Tiles and Tabs

Browsers have grown tabs for twenty years, and yet reading two pages side by side still means juggling windows, dragging edges and losing track of which page belongs to which task.

Tiling changes that. A window splits into tiles, each tile keeps its own tabs, and a page can be dragged from one tile to another, exactly like panes in a good terminal, without a single extra window.

Keeping pages clean

The controls live in small bubbles above the page, never on top of it. Nothing is injected into the page, so what the site draws is what the reader sees, pixel for pixel.

Chrome should explain where things are, and then get out of the way.

Reader view goes one step further, keeping only the text and the pictures of an article, typeset for reading, with the colours of the desktop and a column that is easy on the eyes.

  • Split right or down with a shortcut.
  • Drag a tab onto an edge to make a new tile.
